articles.title: Oil prices seesaw amid renewed diplomatic efforts to end Mideast conflict
articles.summary: Oil prices inched higher Tuesday, reversing earlier losses driven by renewed diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war and hopes of a de-escalation in the wider regional conflict that has seen Tehran-backed Houthis target Saudi Arabia. Prospects of a diplomatic breakthrough have helped temper fears of further disruptions to global energy supplies, putting downward pressure on crude prices.

articles.title: Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta as tech giants deepen AI partnership
articles.summary: Nvidia has said it will invest $3 billion in Meta after the social media and AI giant announced plans to raise $95 billion to support its investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure. Nvidia announced its investment on Tuesday, adding that Meta would expand Vera Rubin and Vera CPU deployment, and that the two companies would deepen their partnership on Muse, the social media giant's AI agent that launched last month.

articles.title: HSBC shares slump on revenue miss, lender announces share buyback of up to $1 billion
articles.summary: Earlier, shares in Hong Kong dropped 2.95% following the earnings release, which saw the bank approve a third interim dividend of 10 cents per share. The bank's net interest income rose to $9.3 billion in the third quarter, supported by deposit growth and reinvestment of its "structural hedge at higher yields." Meanwhile, operating expenses decreased 12% year on year to $8.8 billion, largely due to non-recurrence of legal provisions recorded a year earlier.

articles.title: Opinion: UK bond investors want spending cuts. John Healey’s first Budget may disappoint
articles.summary: The build-up to her annual budgets was scarred by weeks of speculation about which taxes she would raise and, even though some of those increases never materialized, the damage to business and investor confidence was almost as great as if they had been imposed. Other likely giveaways include targeted support for poorer households with energy bills and a higher tax-free allowance for low-income pensioners.

articles.title: The 'stablecoin sandwich': Why speeding up payments isn't so simple, according to Mastercard
articles.summary: Stablecoins could offer faster and more efficient payments, but realizing their full potential requires further development of the infrastructure supporting them, according to Mastercard. dollar, could be attractive for certain remittance corridors and less commonly traded currency pairs, Matthew Driver, executive vice president of services for Asia Pacific at Mastercard, told CNBC in an interview.

articles.title: China industrial profits post strongest growth in three months as tech boom widens economic divide
articles.summary: Earnings growth in high-tech sectors, such as AI and robotics, has been outperforming profits in consumer-related industries, including clothing, autos and furniture, underscoring the increasingly bifurcated momentum in the economy. NBS Chief Statistician Yu Weining attributed earnings growth mostly to surging profits in electronics and advanced-technology manufacturing sectors.

articles.title: China and Russia are redrawing Arctic trade. Can Europe fight back?
articles.summary: For Moscow, the route offers an opportunity to redirect energy exports toward Asia as Western sanctions constrain its access to European markets, said industry watchers whom CNBC spoke to. On the other hand, it provides Beijing another trade artery that could reduce reliance on traditional maritime chokepoints.

articles.title: Bank of Japan is expected to hold rates this week — but stay hawkish: CNBC survey
articles.summary: Japan's core inflation, excluding fresh foods, for September rose 2.1% from a year earlier, reaching its highest this year as a weak yen raises import costs and elevated energy costs feed through to higher prices, even as government subsidies absorb rising costs of energy for consumers.

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO puts power in the hands of founders, giving everyday shareholders little voice
articles.summary: Prospective Anthropic investors better buckle up, because the AI company's seven co-founders are firmly in the driver's seat. The arrangement will also limit the power and influence of institutional and retail investors, who will have to put their trust in a small band of artificial intelligence engineers and researchers as the company marches toward a trillion-dollar-plus market cap.

articles.title: From Wall Street to Silicon Valley, Anthropic IPO poised to have massive 'trickle-down effect'
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available." articles.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI leads to efficiency push
articles.summary: Microsoft said Monday that it's offering buyouts to a wide swath of employees as it strives to balance a costly artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft has been ramping up spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand, supplying cloud services to Anthropic, OpenAI and a slew of other companies.

articles.title: Meta, SpaceX, Anthropic stoke the AI funding frenzy. What it means for our stocks
articles.summary: The AI funding window is closing, and everyone wants a seat on the train. Meta announced plans to raise as much as $95 billion in three steps: first, an additional $22.5 billion worth of Class A common (what we and most investors currently own) priced at $642.62 per share; another $12.5 billion of preferred shares; and $60 billion no sooner than next year via an at-the-market offering for Class C shares.

articles.title: Prediction market traders say an Anthropic IPO is near-certain this year after company filed with SEC
articles.summary: Speculators on prediction market platform Kalshi place 95% odds that the artificial intelligence giant officially announces an initial public offering by the end of 2026. Kalshi defines officially announcing an IPO as either the Securities and Exchange Commission declaring an S-1 effective, a priced IPO or an exchange assigning a ticker to a stock. The Anthropic S-1 envisions a Nasdaq Stock Market ticker symbol of "ANT." Anthropic is aiming to start trading the week of Nov.

articles.title: Federal Reserve is likely to hold interest rates steady in October. Here's what that means for consumers
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming October meeting — even as higher energy costs complicate the inflation outlook and put additional pressure on household budgets. But fed funds futures last priced in less than a 10% chance the central bank will raise rates by another quarter point at its meeting this week, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
